memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The LORD said to Moses, "Give this command to the Israelites and say to them: 'Make sure that you present to me at the appointed time my food offerings, as an aroma pleasing to me.'" - Num 28:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Israel prepared to enter the land, God gave them a calendar of offerings to bring at their appointed times. He calls them "my food offerings, an aroma pleasing to me," language that speaks of communion and delight, though of course God does not need food as we do. The point was that His people would regularly draw near to Him in worship, marking their days and seasons by fellowship with their God.

Before we go further, we should understand these instructions rightly. This was ceremonial law given to Israel under the old covenant. These specific sacrifices are not binding on believers today; they were shadows pointing forward to something greater (Col 2:16-17). We do not offer bulls and lambs, for Christ has fulfilled all that these offerings foreshadowed.

Yet there is timeless truth here. God desired regular, ordered worship from His people, not sporadic or careless devotion. Worship at "the appointed time" was to be a steady rhythm woven through their lives. God still delights when His people draw near to Him consistently, not just in moments of crisis.

The greatest truth is that Christ is the perfect offering, the true aroma pleasing to God. He offered Himself once for all, and through Him we now draw near to God at any time (Eph 5:2). Let this chapter stir you to worship the God who welcomes you, no longer through animal sacrifices but through the finished work of His Son.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a steady rhythm of worship in your life, or only in crisis?
2. How does knowing Christ fulfilled these offerings deepen your worship?
3. What does it mean to draw near to God through Jesus at any time?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Christ is the perfect offering who opened the way for me to draw near. Help me to worship You with a steady, glad devotion, not only in moments of need. Amen.
